Hi Alicia / Ben —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Recap from FinPay call:
- Primary goal: move fraud-detection ranking + customer support routing to a low-latency LLM-backed pipeline.
- Current QPS: ~120 requests/sec average, peak ~450 requests/sec during business hours. Typical prompt lengths ~200 tokens; some flows hit 2k tokens.
- Primary concerns: noisy-neighbor interference on shared infra causing latency spikes, strict isolation for PCI-adjacent workloads, and predictable SLOs for 95th/99th percentiles.

Redwood takeaways:
- Hosted API would be the fastest to get started (no infra to manage) but may have noisy-neighbor variance at very tight P99 targets unless we use our dedicated tiers.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) gives you isolation and predictable throughput — easier to guarantee P95/P99 SLOs and to tune batching/quantization across your workload.
- Private (VPC / on-prem) is available if you need full network isolation or specific compliance requirements.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Tech deep-dive (45–60m) with your infra / security folks + our SE (Marissa) to go over SLO targets, network topology, and the feasibility of a 30-day dedicated pilot.
2) I will share our SOC 2 summary and a sample network diagram for the VPC deployment (see attachments).
3) If we align on SLO targets, we'll propose a pilot capacity plan and an initial pricing/commitment option for Dedicated.

Can you confirm availability for a 45–60m deep-dive Wed or Thurs this week (anytime 10a–3p PT)? If not, propose a couple slots next week.

I'll attach the SOC2 summary and a simple VPC diagram in case your security team wants to review beforehand.

Thanks — looking forward.

— Priyom

Hi Alicia / Ben —

Thanks for setting the time. Quick note ahead of Wednesday's session: 

What I'll cover (10–15m): 
- Isolation modes:
  - Shared (hosted API): best TTV, multi-tenant — some P99 variance due to cross-tenant batching & scheduling.
  - Dedicated (reserved pools): allocated GPUs for your workloads only — consistent latency and throughput, supports strict SLOs, and easier performance debugging.
  - Private (VPC/on-prem): full network and tenancy isolation; necessary when compliance/regulators require dedicated control plane or no egress to shared control plane.

- Noisy-neighbor mitigations we apply for Dedicated: instance pinning, node-level isolation, and workload-aware batch caps. For most customers hitting tight P99s, Dedicated plus prefix caching resolves >95% of incidents.

- Suggested SLOs and error budgets (preview): I'll walk through the attached SLO table. For your P95 < 120ms / P99 < 350ms target, recommended starting configuration is: Dedicated pool sized to ~1.5x peak QPS with autoscale disabled for the pilot (to keep stable tail latency), model pinning to avoid runtime swaps, and a 10% error budget for experiment periods.

Before the call, if you can share the anonymized QPS + token distribution CSV (even a 1-hour sample) that will let us run the capacity sim and bring more concrete numbers to the meeting. If that's sensitive, we can accept aggregate histograms instead.

Looking forward — speak Wednesday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
